controls.label: How it moves
controls.hint: H3 takes a rich prompt — you can describe a timeline, and it generates sound too.

inputs.label: The poster
inputs.note: The artwork as supplied. It is used as both the first and the last frame, so the clip loops and the typography cannot drift.

params.prompt:
Warm evening light, shallow depth of field, unhurried.

Timeline:
[0s-2s] The sign fills the frame, light catching its edge.
[2s-5s] Slow drift back, the street coming into view behind it.

No cuts, no camera shake, no text overlays.

Audio: Low room tone, distant traffic, no music.

presets.label: Bring it to life
presets.hint: The general one. Finds whatever is in the poster and animates each thing plausibly.

values.value:
The image is a finished promotional poster, already designed. Every designed element — the headline, all body text, prices, dates, times, logos, brand marks, panels, borders and flat colour blocks — is graphic furniture, not a subject. It stays exactly where it is, at exactly the same size, perfectly sharp and completely unchanged for the entire clip. No letter re-forms, no word changes, nothing slides, scales or drifts. The camera is locked off, the composition never changes, and the final frame matches the first frame exactly.

Bring the photographed subjects within the artwork to life. Work out what is actually depicted — people, faces, food, drink, fire, water, foliage, fabric, lights, machinery — and give each one the motion it would really have, continuously and independently, as though the poster were a window onto a live scene. Motion is confined to those subjects and to what they naturally affect: their own shadows, reflections and the light falling on them.

Keep every movement small and believable — the kind of motion you would see standing in front of the real scene for five seconds, not a performance. Nothing enters or leaves the frame.

Do not add or alter any text. No new logos, captions, watermarks or subtitles. No transitions, no cuts, no camera movement, no zoom, no pan.
